recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further FHIR-core work is needed for FHIR-55260 unless a later OO decision changes the intended cardinality or packaging-identifier wording.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive OO change request for R6 asking that DeviceDefinition.packaging.identifier repeat because multiple entities can assign identifiers over time; the accepted resolution was to allow multiple identifiers on a packaging instance and update the definition accordingly.
initial_application: Git commit d73d591cb526d1f9386ba83362d1f5e7447d813e applied FHIR-55260 by changing DeviceDefinition.packaging.identifier max from 1 to * and pluralizing the short and definition, plus adding FHIR-55260 to the DeviceDefinition release-note block. No prior AutoFHIR reconciliation commit for FHIR-55260 was present before publishing this audit.
additional_context: DeviceDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/devicedefinition/structuredefinition-DeviceDefinition.xml is in build scope. OO WGM minutes page 413246813 records the 11-0-1 motion and rationale that packages can have multiple identifiers such as serial number and UDI. FHIR-54860 is a same-element wording correction from packaged medication to packaged device and is background for the current wording; no conflicting Zulip discussion was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current in-scope source already has DeviceDefinition.packaging.identifier with max value="*" and plural "Business identifiers of the packaged device" wording.

related_jiras.note: Separate applied issue on the same element corrected the old packaged-medication wording to packaged-device wording before FHIR-55260 pluralized it; it supports the current-source interpretation but was not decided by this seed audit.
